biggest_catch: Only about 2% of applicants pass vetting — and winning freelance engagements is competitive, never guaranteed.
catches: Strict vetting — only about the top 2% of applicants pass.
Winning engagements is competitive and never guaranteed.
Rates vary by engagement; the $60–100+/hr figure is Arc's stated typical range, not a promise.
Arc's free job-posting tier exposes only non-vetted developers (client-side detail; vetted talent is the paid tier).

c1.evidence: Arc's own site describes the vetted-developer marketplace: developers pass screening and interviews, then 'become eligible to get featured to companies' hiring freelance developers — a real, public deal channel.

c2.evidence: Arc's hiring-side guide cites typical client rates of $60–100+/hour, but no fixed provider pay range is disclosed — framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: profile, vetting (screening + interviews), featured to companies, interviews, engagement.

c4.evidence: Developer signup and vetting carry no upfront fee; Arc monetizes the hiring side.

eligibility: Developers who can pass profile screening and behavioral plus technical interviews; remote-friendly.
notes: Scenario: dev niche (vetted remote developers). Arc is a vetted developer network: engineers pass screening and interviews, then get matched to freelance and full-time roles. Highly selective; engagements and pay are variable — never guaranteed.
numeric_basis: payout: per-engagement, no official fixed provider range. time: 60 min of billable work to earn one hour's pay, up to 120 min including vetting/matching overhead.

Get featured to companies hiring freelance, full-time, or contract developers.
Interview with matched companies; Arc states freelance placements can close in about 72 hours.
Work the engagement; Arc's own guide states freelance developers typically charge $60–100+/hour.
